title: Gate-Level Trojan Suspect-Node Localization in a Synthesized AES-like Netlist
summary: Analyze a small gate-level Verilog netlist of a synthesized AES-like datapath block, determine whether it is infected with a hardware Trojan, and if so, localize the suspect trigger/payload gate instances and the affected primary output.
submission_contract: Participants do not modify files under inputs/. They write a single JSON analysis report to submission/trojan_report.json. A starter (naive) submission is already present at that path and is expected to fail grading; it must be replaced with a real analysis.

expected_outputs.description: A single JSON object at submission/trojan_report.json with top-level keys: 'infected' (boolean), 'suspect_nodes' (array of exact gate/wire instance names from inputs/aes_sub_netlist.v), 'rationale' (non-empty string explaining the structural/functional reasoning), and 'primary_output_affected' (string matching an output port name from inputs/port_map.json, or empty string if 'infected' is false).

metrics.name: detection_rate
metrics.description: Fraction of security requirements correctly satisfied by the submitted trojan_report.json relative to hidden ground truth, focused on correct identification of infection status, suspect trigger/payload nodes, and affected primary output.

metrics.name: false_positive_rate
metrics.description: Fraction of submitted suspect_nodes entries that do not correspond to any real Trojan-related instance (spurious accusations against benign gates).

metrics.name: inference_latency
metrics.description: Wall-clock time (seconds) taken by the evaluator to parse and grade the submitted report, including any optional yosys/iverilog/vvp cross-check simulation.
